newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares back on record track after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: German shares back on record track after U.S. data.

text.p: German shares vaulted over old record highs on Friday afternoon in the wake of a fresh surge by Bunds on reassuring U.S. economic data and were broadly seen back on track to chase new records next week.

Low staffing after the May Day holiday on Thursday was keeping activity modest in Germany on Friday and dealers said more buy orders should come in on Monday, especially as recent dividend payouts boosted liquidity.
The 30-share IBIS DAX was up 32.48 points at 3,470.35 at 1310 GMT, having spiked to a new all-time high of 3,504.27 points after the release of U.S. April payrolls data.
The last record set on the IBIS DAX was 3,475.18, reached on March 11.
While the initial boost provided by the U.S. appeared to have worn off, a Stuttgart dealer predicted a retesting of the 3,500 point DAX level next week.
"This is not over yet, although it remains to be seen what happens on the Dow Jones," he said.
Volatility was inevitable given that trading volumes were so low, the trader added.
Volkswagen continued its surge in afternoon trade and was up 5.6 percent at 1,157 marks.
Dealers could not identify one particular reason for VW's gains, other than several large buy orders, but noted that cars in general were popular because of the dollar's strength against the mark.
"The auto sector is simply in vogue at the moment," said one dealer.
Daimler Benz AG was up 4.2 percent at 133.55 marks.
Drugs group Schering AG extended gains sparked on Wednesday after the company said it planned to buy back its own shares once German law allowed.
The shares were up 4.50 marks at 170 marks in the late trade.
Dealers said dividend payout season in the chemicals sector should bring more liquidity into the market. Schering and Bayer paid dividends this week.

Interesting corporate news next week includes first quarter results from Hoechst AG on Monday and airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG's annual news conference on Monday, which is expected to yield details on its dividend plans.
